gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/insn.rs::Insn::Filter + Insn::FilterAdd (bloom-filter build/probe pair)
gaps.notes: Turso builds a bloom filter over a join/IN side and probes it to skip btree seeks. Ahtola has no bloom machinery. NAME COLLISION: Ahtola's VdbeOpcode.Filter (12) is a row-predicate filter (VdbeRowPredicate delegate), NOT the bloom-filter probe — any port must rename. Pure optimization: results stay correct without it.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/insn.rs::Insn::HashBuild, HashDistinct, HashBuildFinalize, HashProbe, HashNext, HashClose, HashClear, HashMarkMatched, HashResetMatched, HashScanUnmatched, HashNextUnmatched, HashGraceInit, HashLoadPartition, HashNextProbe, HashAdvancePartition (16 opcodes; turso-src/core/vdbe/hash_table.rs)
gaps.notes: Entire hash-join execution family absent, including the grace (disk-partitioned) variant for outsized build sides and the unmatched-scan support for outer joins. Ahtola joins are in-memory nested loops over materialized rows (VdbeJoinPlan/OpenJoinCursor), so large equijoins degrade. The triple-selfjoin conformance timeouts are planner-caused (no cost-based ordering) but hash join is the execution-side fix.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/insn.rs::Insn::VOpen, VFilter, VColumn, VNext, VUpdate, VDestroy, VBegin, VRename (turso-src/core/vtab.rs)
gaps.notes: No virtual-table opcode family at all: modules cannot be opened, filtered with constraint push-down (xBestIndex), column-read, updated, or renamed. Blocks the entire eponymous/module vtab SQL surface. All 5 vtab conformance failures trace here (parser accepts CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE per parser-layer entry, execution cannot run it).

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/insn.rs::Insn::Program, Gosub, Return, BeginSubrtn (trigger/FK sub-program invocation and subroutine call/return)
gaps.notes: No subprogram or subroutine machinery: triggers cannot fire from compiled DML because there is no Program opcode to invoke a sub-program with its own register frame, and no Gosub/Return for shared code blocks. Ahtola programs are straight-line with explicit targets; subroutines are inlined at compile time. Prerequisite for any trigger support.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/execute.rs::op_halt (err_code + description + on_error + description_reg for RAISE); op_halt_if_null
gaps.ahtola_ref: src/Ahtola.Core/Execution/ResumableStatement.cs (case HaltInstruction, ~line 1139: clean stop, cursor cleanup only)
gaps.notes: Turso's Halt terminates with a SQLite error code, message, and on_error disposition (abort/ignore/fail), and HaltIfNull raises constraint errors from NULL registers (RAISE, NOT NULL). Ahtola's HaltInstruction only stops cleanly; all errors propagate as .NET exceptions (EmbeddedSqlException/VdbeArithmeticException) and are mapped to SQLite codes at the provider boundary (SqliteException.SqliteErrorCode). Works for top-level errors but cannot express in-program error recovery (ON CONFLICT CONTINUE semantics inside a program) or RAISE().

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/execute.rs::op_transaction (read/write flag, schema-cookie check, statement-tx sub-state machine); op_autocommit
gaps.notes: Different factoring, verified semantics: Ahtola splits into Begin/Commit/Rollback opcodes over VdbeTransaction (register-snapshot stack) with savepoint trio Savepoint/Release/RollbackTo mapping Turso's single Savepoint opcode with op enum. NAME COLLISION: Ahtola's VdbeOpcode.Commit is a cursor-write flush (returns LastInsertRowId), not a transaction commit. Isolation/atomicity gaps are in the mvcc layer entries, not here.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/execute.rs::Insn::OpenEphemeral, OpenAutoindex (execute.rs ~line 13467), OpenPseudo, OpenDup
gaps.notes: No general-purpose ephemeral btree opcode: Turso materializes IN (...) sets, DISTINCT intermediates, subquery results, and auto-indexes into ephemeral tables with full cursor semantics (seek/scan). Ahtola's only ephemeral store is the recursive-CTE work table; IN-list materialization and subquery materialization fall back to in-memory arrays/delegates, which caps planner options (no ephemeral index over a materialized subquery). OpenPseudo/OpenDup are minor conveniences Ahtola does not need structurally.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/insn.rs::Insn::OpenAutoindex + translate/optimizer (automatic transient index over the inner side of a join)
gaps.notes: Turso can build a transient auto-index when no usable index exists for a join. Combined with the missing cost-based join order (compilation entry), Ahtola's joins are O(N*M) nested loops with materialized right sides.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/execute.rs::op_deferred_seek (line 5180) + op_seek_end (line 5739); op_column OpColumnState::Rowid/Seek deferred path (lines 1779-1833)
gaps.notes: DeferredSeek lets an index scan postpone the table-btree seek until a column outside the index is actually read (covering-index fast path); SeekEnd positions a cursor past the last row for append workloads. Ahtola always materializes the full row on cursor access (CurrentCursorRow), so there is no covering-index read path and no lazy seek.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/execute.rs::Insn::IdxGE, IdxGT, IdxLE, IdxLT (execute.rs ~line 5680), IdxRowId, IdxInsert (line 10499), IdxDelete (line 10380), RowData
gaps.ahtola_ref: src/Ahtola.Core/Compilation/SortedScanProgramBuilder.cs; index maintenance inside write-target delegates (no dedicated opcodes)
gaps.notes: Turso has a full index-cursor family: range seeks with eq_only over index records, rowid extraction from index entries, index insert/delete with IdxInsertFlags (no-op dup detection), and raw record access (RowData). Ahtola reaches indexes only through the SortedScan builder and maintains them inside DML delegates. Works for the compiled shapes but blocks index-only scans, IN-driven index seeks, and partial/expression index exploitation (see compilation entries).

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/execute.rs::Insn::SeekGE, SeekGT, SeekLE, SeekLT with eq_only (lines 5232-5300); Insn::Found, NotFound, NoConflict, NotExists
gaps.notes: Ahtola consolidates point seeks into SeekRowid (with Found/NotFound targets folded in — a faithful merge of SeekRowid+Found/NotFound) and has SeekRowidRange for rowid ranges, but has no record-key seeks (SeekGE/GT/LE/LT over arbitrary index keys) and no eq_only distinction, and no NoConflict/NotExists probe opcodes (uniqueness is enforced inside write delegates instead). SeekRowidInstruction's own doc comment notes its scaffolding 'is not yet emitted by SelectStatementCompiler' — the opcode exists but the compiler never uses it (dead opcode today).

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/insn.rs::Insn::RowSetTest (dedup probe: jump if rowid already in set)
gaps.notes: Ahtola's RowSet trio maps Turso's RowSetAdd/RowSetRead (insert + drain) but lacks RowSetTest, the membership probe used to deduplicate rowids from OR'd index scans. Without it, multi-index OR plans cannot dedup — consistent with the compilation-layer finding that OR-index-union plans are absent.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/execute.rs::op_make_record (line 2746: serial-type encoding into SQLite record format); op_type_check (line 2023)
gaps.ahtola_ref: src/Ahtola.Core/Execution (registers hold SqlValue[] rows; record encoding happens at the pager write boundary); src/Ahtola.Core/Execution/VdbeProgram.cs::NumericAffinityInstruction, CastInstruction
gaps.notes: No MakeRecord: Ahtola rows live as materialized SqlValue arrays end-to-end and are only encoded to SQLite record format by the pager when a page is written. Format parity is a storage-layer concern (verified there); the VDBE-level consequence is that affinity-on-write (Turso's TypeCheck applying column affinities + CHECKs to a record before insert) happens in Ahtola's write delegates instead — see vdbe-typecheck-on-write.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/execute.rs::op_type_check (applies column affinities to a register block and enforces CHECK constraints before MakeRecord/Insert)
gaps.notes: Closed 2026-08-03 via four coordinated fixes. (A) ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN on a STRICT table now rejects a type-mismatched DEFAULT with 'type mismatch on DEFAULT' (existing rows only), matching SQLite instead of the row-level 'cannot store X value in Y column'. (B) i64 cast boundaries made exclusive at all six sites: a float exactly at i64::MIN/MAX (or beyond) no longer wraps, it errors 'integer overflow' per SQLite's cast semantics. (C) Comparison-affinity threading through a QueryContext: rowid and rowid-alias column references carry Integer affinity in comparisons (including IN lists via ApplyInComparisonAffinity), while NEW/OLD trigger pseudo-table columns carry NO affinity except rowid aliases and the rowid register, exactly per turso-src/core/translate/trigger_exec.rs:1043-1070 (SQLite forum 819f2d6627). (D) TRIM/LTRIM/RTRIM and nth_value boundary parsing now treat only ASCII whitespace as trimmable, so Unicode-space-padded values stay intact (SQLite trim is ASCII-only). Expected-failures count dropped by 13 (12 mapped + nth-value-unicode-whitespace-n-errors) with zero additions; full lane 3765/3765 passing. Two cases previously linked here (subquery-column-affinity-inheritance, range-scan-text-vs-int-affinity) are affinity-propagation issues in subquery/compound contexts and now track under compile-affinity-rules-diverge-in-subquery-and-compound-contexts; the two gencol_self_table_affinity_indexed_* cases were already closed by parser-indexed-by-hint.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/insn.rs::Insn::NewRowid (max+1 allocation with random-retry fallback at i64::MAX; separate from last_insert_rowid tracking)
gaps.ahtola_ref: src/Ahtola.Core/Execution/ResumableStatement.cs (CommitInstruction: LastInsertRowId = target.Commit(), ~line 631); rowid allocation inside write targets
gaps.notes: Rowid allocation is delegated to the write target's Commit rather than a NewRowid opcode. The autoinc failure (explicit max-rowid insert followed by plain INSERT) suggests the allocation edge (SQLite falls back to random unused rowid when max is reached; AUTOINCREMENT must error instead) is not faithfully reproduced. Verify SQLITE_FULL-vs-random behavior when porting.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/execute.rs::op_insert (line 9897: InsertFlags::REQUIRE_SEEK, UPDATE_ROWID_CHANGE, PREFER_UPDATE; old-record capture for dependent views); op_delete (line 10274)
gaps.notes: Ahtola models UPDATE as its own opcode plus delegate mutation, with change counting present. Missing flag semantics: REQUIRE_SEEK (position-before-write), UPDATE_ROWID_CHANGE (rowid-changing UPDATE ordering), PREFER_UPDATE (upsert resolution hint). The MVCC-layer finding that statement-level rollback after ON CONFLICT ROLLBACK on UPDATE is broken compounds here: conflict disposition is decided inside delegates with no flag channel.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/execute.rs::op_comparison (line 888: Eq/Ne/Lt/Le/Gt/Ge as direct conditional jumps with CmpInsFlags {null_eq, jump_if_null, affinity, collation})
gaps.notes: Verified near-parity consolidation: Ahtola evaluates the comparison to a tri-state value (IS/IS NOT handled null-safely; NULL -> NULL; affinities applied per side; collation passed) then branches on IsTrue. jump_if_null maps to NULL->false->FalseTarget; null_eq maps to the IS operator. Residual risks: (1) EmbeddedDatabase.IsTrue throws 'datatype mismatch' for non-numeric text where SQLite treats it as false; (2) JumpIfInstruction (~line 693) silently treats text as not-jumping — inconsistent with IsTrue. Recorded for completeness; fix the two IsTrue edges rather than de-consolidating.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/insn.rs::Insn::Column { default } / execute.rs::op_column
gaps.notes: Closed 2026-08-08. Turso's Column instruction supplies its constant default P4 for a short pre-ALTER record. Ahtola performs the equivalent once while materializing a file-backed row: ReadTableRow detects fewer stored fields than the current non-generated schema and fills each missing trailing field from EmbeddedColumn.DefaultValue (or NULL). ManagedAddColumnShortRowTests covers SQLite-authored database reads with NULL and constant defaults, several sequential additions, NOT NULL defaults, WITHOUT ROWID tables, and managed writes before validating the resulting file with ordinary SQLite.

The managed engine commits inline, so main checkpoints report 0|0|0; temp has no WAL and correctly reports 0|-1|-1. The temp-schema corpus case passes. This is behavioral parity through the evaluator path rather than a separate VDBE Checkpoint instruction.

gaps.notes: Ahtola has a real EXPLAIN implementation over its own opcode set, so output necessarily diverges from SQLite/Turso text (different opcode names, no p1-p5 operand columns). Acceptable while EXPLAIN is diagnostic-only, but any conformance case asserting EXPLAIN output shape or EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN rows will fail. Decide policy: SQLite-emulating output vs documented Ahtola dialect.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/execute.rs::{apply_kbn_step,apply_kbn_step_int,update_agg_payload,finalize_agg_payload}; core/vdbe/execute.rs::handle_text_sum
gaps.notes: Closed 2026-08-08. SUM/TOTAL/AVG now share a Kahan-Babuska-Neumaier accumulator in evaluator and compiled VDBE paths. Numeric::Integer SUM overflow faults from AggStep before later source rows execute; TOTAL and AVG promote to compensated REAL accumulation. The separate text-conversion path still promotes a text integer overflow, and NaN/infinite cancellation reaches SQL NULL. NumericAggregateParityTests covers compensated precision, infinities, empty inputs, and text/numeric coercion; TursoAggregateStepParityTests proves overflow timing with a side-effecting scalar. No active expected-failure key was linked.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/translate/optimizer/join.rs::optimize_join_order (System R style DP), turso-src/core/translate/optimizer/mod.rs::optimize_plan
gaps.notes: Turso's optimizer/join.rs implements a System-R style dynamic-programming join reordering algorithm with pruning, using per-table cost/cardinality estimates (optimizer/cost.rs, cost_params.rs) and ANALYZE stats when present. Ahtola's VdbeJoinPlan always joins tables strictly in FROM/JOIN clause order (VdbeJoinOperatorPlan is a fixed left-deep tree built by the caller, not re-ordered by any cost model). Multi-table queries where writing the FROM clause in join order matters for performance will be correct but slow; there is no code path that reorders joins for a smaller intermediate result.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/translate/optimizer/access_method.rs::best_access_method, turso-src/core/translate/optimizer/constraints.rs
gaps.notes: Turso extracts WHERE-clause conjuncts into per-table Constraints and picks the cheapest access method (rowid seek, single/multi-column index seek, or full scan) per table independently of join order, considering multiple candidate indexes and their selectivity. Ahtola's ResolveScanTarget/IndexSemantics resolve at most one usable index per scan target via direct predicate-to-index matching (IndexExpressionSemantics.PredicateImplies/SplitConjuncts); there is no comparison between competing candidate indexes on the same table, no partial-index-aware cost comparison, and no multi-index intersection (Turso's optimizer/multi_index.rs, OR-clause index union) at all.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/translate/optimizer/multi_index.rs
gaps.notes: SQLite/Turso can satisfy `WHERE a=1 OR b=2` (with separate indexes on a and b) via an index-union/OR-optimization instead of a full scan. Ahtola's compiler has no equivalent: OR predicates in WHERE fall back to sequential scan filtering (FilterRegistersInstruction), never index lookups per OR-branch.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/translate/optimizer/order.rs::eliminate_order_by, turso-src/core/translate/order_by.rs
gaps.notes: Turso's order.rs decides, per join order and access method, whether the chosen index already produces the required ORDER BY/GROUP BY order and elides the sort step. Ahtola only special-cases a single ORDER BY term matching the primary key/rowid for a single-table backward scan (SelectStatementCompiler ~line 132); any other case -- including index-satisfied ORDER BY on a secondary index, or GROUP BY order elision -- always materializes through a Sorter (SortedScanProgramBuilder). The listed conformance failures show sort-elision expectations not met for window/CTE queries. (Previously linked keys cleared by earlier wave work: window-partial-not-elided, window-no-cte-order-not-elided.)

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/translate/select.rs (join emission uses per-node OpenRead/Seek via chosen access method)
gaps.notes: VdbeJoinOperatorPlan.Enumerate always materializes the right side fully and nested-loops the left side against it in memory (VdbeJoinRow arrays), regardless of whether an index exists on the join key. There is no index-driven nested-loop join (seek into the right table per left row using its index) anywhere in the join plan machinery -- every N-way join is O(preceding-rows * table-size) in the worst case. JoinProgramBuilder.cs (2-table direct builder) is explicitly nested-loop only per its own doc comment.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/translate/optimizer/access_method.rs, cost.rs (equi-join cost modeling; Turso does not implement a hash-join operator either, but its cost model reasons about equi-join constraints for index seeks)
gaps.notes: Neither engine implements a true hash-join operator (both fundamentally rely on nested-loop plus index seeks), so this is not a gap versus Turso per se, but flagged because Ahtola's total absence of index-driven joins (see compile-nway-join-not-index-driven) means large equi-joins have no efficient path at all, whereas Turso's cost model at least picks an index seek that approximates hash-join performance for the common case.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/translate/subquery.rs (recursive CTE planning, multiple recursive terms via compound UNION legs), turso-src/core/translate/compound_select.rs
gaps.notes: RecursiveCteProgramBuilder explicitly documents its scope as "the well-defined linear recursion (a single recursive transform)" and states "Multiple distinct recursive terms ... and mutual recursion are out of scope". `WITH RECURSIVE cte AS (anchor UNION leg1 UNION leg2 ...)` (3+ compound terms) fails to parse/compile ("Expected RightParen"), confirmed by the cte_expressions.sqltest failures. (Previously linked keys cleared by earlier wave work: cte-multi-union, cte-union-all-with-duplicates.)

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/translate/subquery.rs, planner.rs (FROM-clause subquery flattening / pull-up into the outer query)

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/sqlite/parser/src/parser.rs::result_column (nm without AS)
gaps.notes: SQLite (and turso-parser's result_column grammar) allows a SELECT-list column alias with or without the AS keyword: `SELECT 1 a, 2 b`. Ahtola's ParseProjection (SqlParser.cs:1794-1819) only calls ConsumeKeyword("AS") before ExpectIdentifier for the alias; if AS is omitted the trailing identifier is left unconsumed and the enclosing subquery/CTE/paren context fails with a generic 'Expected RightParen'/'Expected End' error at the alias token's offset. This single omission accounts for the large majority of the ~78 'Expected X. At SQL offset N' expected-failure group: every sqltest that uses the extremely common `expr alias` idiom inside a derived table, CTE, or nested subquery breaks.       Verified by hand-computing the failing offset in half a dozen distinct failures (all land exactly on the bare alias identifier). Closed 2026-08-03: ParseProjection now accepts SQLite-style elided column aliases (`SELECT expr alias`) using SQLite's reserved-word set to bound aliasability, with a numeric-adjacency guard so glued literals like `SELECT 0xFF__FF` still error as SQLite's tokenizer requires. Conformance net: 36 mapped cases cleared outright (cte*, subquery/expressions, window checksums, agg infinity cases); 5 mapped cases redistributed to their next blocker (window FILTER clause, aggregate-in-GROUP-BY/ORDER-BY misuse, ctas schema literals).

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/sqlite/parser/src/ast.rs::Expr::IsNull / NotNull (postfix ISNULL/NOTNULL/NOT NULL)
gaps.ahtola_ref: src/Ahtola.Core/Parsing/SqlParser.cs::ParseComparison (postfix ISNULL/NOTNULL/NOT NULL lowered to IS/IS NOT NULL)
gaps.notes: SQLite's expr grammar has three null-test postfix forms: `expr ISNULL`, `expr NOTNULL`, and `expr NOT NULL` (all equivalent to `expr IS [NOT] NULL`). Ahtola's parser has no ISNULL/NOTNULL keyword handling at all, and its NOT-postfix branch only recognizes BETWEEN/IN/LIKE/GLOB/REGEXP/MATCH after NOT — the literal error thrown is 'Expected BETWEEN, IN, LIKE, GLOB, REGEXP, or MATCH after NOT.' when NULL follows NOT.       This rejects extremely common SQL (`x ISNULL`, `x NOT NULL` as an expression) both at the top level and inside generated-column expressions. Fixed 2026-08-03: ParseComparison now parses postfix ISNULL/NOTNULL right after the IS arm and lowers them to BinaryExpression(Is|IsNot, LiteralExpression(SqlValue.Null)) — byte-equivalent compilation to IS NULL / IS NOT NULL — and postfix `expr NOT NULL` is accepted via the postfix-NOT machinery, matching Turso's precedence (comparison level, tighter than prefix NOT, so `1 ISNULL AND 1` = 0). All 8 mapped keys removed from managed-sqltest-expected-failures.txt; full lane 3765/3765.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/sqlite/parser/src/lexer.rs (numeric literal scanning permits `_` digit-group separators, e.g. `9_223_372_036_854_775_807`)
gaps.notes: SQLite 3.46+ / Turso's lexer accepts `_` as a digit-group separator anywhere inside an integer or real literal (`9_223_372_036_854_775_807`, `1_2_3`), which is stripped before parsing the numeric value. Ahtola's ReadNumber only loops over `char.IsAsciiDigit(_sql[_offset])` for the integer part, fractional part, and exponent, with no `_` handling in any of the three loops, so any underscore in a numeric literal terminates the token early and the remaining digits are re-lexed as a separate (invalid) token, producing 'Expected End'. Closed 2026-08-03: ReadNumber now consumes `_` between digits via ConsumeDigitRun (hex, integer, fraction, and exponent runs) and strips separators from the token text via NumericLiteralText so downstream value parsing sees the canonical digits; a separator lacking a digit before or after throws at lex time, matching Turso's BadNumber. SqlParser.TryParseOrderByOrdinal normalizes separators so `ORDER BY 1_0` resolves as ordinal 10. Expected-failures net: exactly the 9 mapped keys removed, 0 added; full lane 3765/3765 green.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/storage/btree.rs::balance, balance_non_root, balance_quick, balance_root
gaps.notes: SqliteBtreeSplitMutation's own doc comment states it 'can replace existing pages or append new pages, but never shrinks, rebalances, or reclaims pages.' Turso implements full B-tree balancing (redistribute cells across up to 3 siblings, merge underfull pages, promote/collapse the root). Ahtola only ever grows pages via leaf split; there is no sibling rebalancing or interior-page merge path. Over time this produces ever-growing, increasingly unbalanced trees and pages that never shrink back after bulk deletes, and is the root cause of several other gaps in this list (freelist reuse, defragmentation, incremental vacuum).

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/storage/pager.rs::Pager::allocate_page (ReuseFreelistLeaf state machine)
gaps.notes: Ahtola's only page allocator is SqliteAppendOnlyPageAllocator, whose doc comment says it 'does not inspect or reclaim the SQLite freelist' and always assigns new page numbers past the current end of file. Turso's Pager::allocate_page consults the freelist trunk chain first (ReuseFreelistLeaf state) before growing the file. Practical effect: every DELETE/DROP in Ahtola leaves file space that is never reused by subsequent INSERTs outside of a full VACUUM rewrite, so the main database file only ever grows (bloat), unlike stock SQLite/Turso.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/storage/pager.rs::Pager::free_page, ReuseFreelistLeaf, NEW_FREELIST_TRUNK
gaps.notes: SqliteFreelist.cs correctly parses and can construct trunk/leaf freelist pages, but per its own doc comment it is used only by 'managed file rewrites' (i.e. VACUUM-style full reconstruction), not by the normal DML write path. There is no free_page()-equivalent invoked when a b-tree page becomes empty during ordinary DELETE/DROP TABLE transactions, so the freelist is only ever populated/consumed as a side effect of a full rewrite, not incrementally as SQLite/Turso do.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/storage/pager.rs::AutoVacuumMode::Incremental, ptrmap_get/ptrmap_put; turso-src/core/vdbe/vacuum.rs::reject_unsupported_vacuum_auto_vacuum_mode
gaps.notes: No AutoVacuumMode/ptrmap concept exists anywhere in Ahtola.Core (grep for 'autovacuum'/'ptrmap' finds nothing outside SQL parsing/authorization text). Turso itself only partially supports this (Full auto-vacuum has ptrmap plumbing, but vacuum.rs explicitly rejects AutoVacuumMode::Incremental as unsupported), so full parity is not required, but Ahtola is missing even the header-level auto_vacuum flag storage and the ptrmap page format entirely. PRAGMA incremental_vacuum / auto_vacuum are effectively no-ops storage-side, independent of the PRAGMA-parsing gap owned by another layer.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/storage/page_cache.rs::PageCache::needs_spill, SpillResult, DEFAULT_SPILL_THRESHOLD_PERCENT
gaps.notes: SqlitePagerReadCache is a plain bounded LRU cache for clean committed pages only (no dirty-page tracking, no spill-threshold, no PagesToSpill/CacheFull semantics). Turso's PageCache tracks dirty vs. evictable pages, computes a spill threshold (90% of capacity by default) and can proactively spill dirty pages mid-transaction so large transactions do not exceed cache_size. Ahtola has no equivalent dirty-page spilling at all -- this is the concrete storage-side cause of the ~10 'Unsupported PRAGMA cache_size/cache_spill' conformance failures another agent's PRAGMA-parsing fix cannot resolve alone.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/storage/btree.rs::defragment_page, defragment_page_fast, defragment_page_full, defragment_page_for_insert
gaps.notes: No defragment_page equivalent exists in Ahtola's b-tree page writers. Repeated insert/delete of variable-length cells on the same page will fragment free space within the page (gaps between cells) with no in-page compaction pass, forcing premature splits/allocations sooner than stock SQLite/Turso would. Not a format violation (page remains a valid, if fragmented, SQLite page) but a capacity/perf regression.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/storage/wal.rs::CheckpointMode (Passive, Full, Restart, Truncate)
gaps.notes: Not a gap -- included for completeness of the checkpoint-mode audit. Ahtola's SqliteWalCheckpointMode enum (Passive/Full/Restart/Truncate) mirrors Turso's CheckpointMode variants, and SqliteWalWriterCheckpointCoordinator implements busy-handler-style backfill accounting (SafeFrame/BackfilledFrameCount) analogous to Turso's CheckpointResult. Marked as parity, not a discovered defect.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/storage/wal.rs::TursoRwLock, WalConnectionState, ShmWalCoordination locking (READ_LOCK(n)/WRITE_LOCK/CHECKPOINT_LOCK byte ranges)
gaps.notes: SqliteWalByteRangeLock/SqliteWalSharedMemoryLocks implement the -shm byte-range lock offsets for the primary main-database WAL (read marks, write lock, checkpoint lock), giving good format-level parity for the common case. However, the coordinator itself documents (SqliteWalWriterCheckpointCoordinator remarks) that it 'neither acquires nor relaxes the managed pager's Stage 0 main-file ownership lock,' i.e. these primitives are a detached/offline protocol layer, not the live in-process pager's own concurrent-access lock manager, and multi-attached/temp-database WAL locking is called out as a known conformance gap. This is a scope gap versus Turso's unified Wal trait locking across every attached database, not a byte-offset format bug.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/storage/pager.rs (rollback/journal recovery on open), turso-src/core/storage/sqlite3_ondisk.rs
gaps.notes: SqliteRollbackJournal.IsHot detects a stale/hot rollback journal from a crashed writer, but the recovery path is a narrow helper (journal-mode enum + hot-detection + apply) rather than the full pager-integrated hot-journal replay Turso performs on every database open (validating journal header magic/page count/checksums, replaying each journal page, then deleting/truncating the journal, all before any reader is allowed access). Needs verification that partial/corrupt journals, super-journals (master journal for multi-file transactions), and journal_mode=PERSIST/TRUNCATE variants are all covered; multi-database (ATTACH) super-journal recovery does not appear to be implemented.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/storage/pager.rs (master/super-journal path for multi-file atomic commit)
gaps.notes: No super-journal (a.k.a. master journal) file handling was found in SqliteRollbackJournal.cs or elsewhere in Storage/. Stock SQLite/Turso use a super-journal to atomically commit rollback-journal-mode transactions spanning multiple ATTACHed databases. Ahtola's rollback-journal support appears scoped to a single main database file only.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/storage/buffer_pool.rs::BufferPool, ArenaBuffer, Arena (slab/arena page-buffer allocator with try_alloc/free)
gaps.notes: Turso maintains a dedicated arena-based BufferPool that recycles fixed-size page/WAL-frame buffers to avoid per-page heap allocation churn under concurrent I/O. Ahtola has no equivalent pooling abstraction in Storage/ -- page images appear to be plain managed byte[] arrays allocated per read/write (see SqlitePagerReadCache.Entry(byte[] Page, ...) and SqliteFreelist's `new byte[pageSize]`). This is a GC-pressure/perf gap, not a correctness gap, given .NET's managed heap.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/storage/encryption.rs::EncryptionKey, CipherMode (AES-128/256-GCM, AEGIS family)
gaps.notes: Intentional Ahtola extension per task context (kind=extension, s4-intentional). gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/storage/wal.rs::VacuumLockGuard, CheckpointLocks (guards preventing VACUUM/checkpoint races)

Ahtola's coordinator manages Write/Checkpoint/Recovery/FirstReadMark lock offsets but, given the append-only allocator and lack of an incremental-vacuum/full-rewrite integration point in Storage/, there is no equivalent explicit vacuum-vs-checkpoint mutual exclusion guard visible. Worth a targeted concurrency test once/if a non-append-only allocator or incremental vacuum is added, since the two subsystems (checkpoint backfill positions and any future page-relocating vacuum) would otherwise race on the same PageStore.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/mvcc/mod.rs, turso-src/core/mvcc/database/mod.rs::MvStore, RowVersion, Transaction, TransactionState, turso-src/core/mvcc/clock.rs::MvccClock, turso-src/core/mvcc/cursor.rs, turso-src/core/mvcc/persistent_storage/logical_log.rs
gaps.notes: Turso implements a full main-memory MVCC engine (Larson et al., VLDB 2011) alongside its classic SQLite-compatible pager/b-tree path, selected per-transaction via `BEGIN CONCURRENT` (see execute.rs::begin_mvcc_tx, TransactionMode::Concurrent) rather than a global PRAGMA. Core pieces: (1) MvStore (database/mod.rs, ~10k lines) owns an in-memory multi-version row store keyed by RowID, with RowVersion carrying begin_ts/end_ts (TxTimestampOrID) and a RowVersionState (Committed/Uncommitted/Aborted-like states); (2) MvccClock (clock.rs) is a mutex-guarded logical clock generating monotonically increasing begin/commit timestamps, with a documented 'speculative reads' protocol so an active tx can observe another tx's writes once it enters the Preparing state even before it fully commits (atomicity between get_timestamp and publishing the Preparing state closes a TOCTOU snapshot-isolation hole the maintainers hit once already); (3) first-committer-wins conflict detection returns LimboError::WriteWriteConflict on commit when a concurrent writer touched the same row, so the caller must retry/rollback (see the busy-retry loops in mvcc/mod.rs tests); (4) a dual cursor (cursor.rs, MvccCursorType::Table/Index) that transparently overlays the MVCC version store on top of the classic b-tree cursor, promoting a plain btree cursor into an MVCC-aware one lazily (execute.rs::maybe_promote_to_mvcc_cursor); (5) a logical_log persistent_storage layer (persistent_storage/logical_log.rs, ~8k lines) that durably logs the version store's operations rather than paging rows through the WAL directly, plus a checkpoint_state_machine (database/checkpoint_state_machine.rs) that periodically folds the logical log into the b-tree/WAL so a restart can rebuild the MVCC store; (6) garbage collection via drop_unused_row_versions[/_and_slots] which prunes row versions no longer visible to any active transaction, invoked opportunistically from the commit path. Isolation level is snapshot isolation with read-your-writes and dirty-write/dirty-read prevention by construction (version visibility check before update), but the module's own doc header states phantom reads, cursor lost updates, read skew, and write skew are explicit unresolved TODOs upstream, and optimistic reads/writes plus GC are still marked incomplete even in the reference implementation. Two data paths coexist per-connection: ordinary BEGIN/BEGIN IMMEDIATE/BEGIN DEFERRED still go through the pager/WAL/b-tree exactly as classic SQLite; only BEGIN CONCURRENT engages MvStore, and mixing the two on the same table within one process requires the promotion/cursor-overlay machinery so a concurrent reader on a b-tree cursor does NOT see an uncommitted MVCC writer's row (test_mvcc_dual_cursor_transaction_isolation demonstrates this explicitly: a second BEGIN CONCURRENT connection sees the pre-MVCC-commit b-tree value, not the in-flight MVCC value). Ahtola has zero equivalent: no `*Mvcc*.cs` file exists anywhere in src/, `BEGIN CONCURRENT` is not a recognized parser production (fails with a generic 'Expected End' parse error per the conformance corpus), and every transaction — read or write — goes through the single pager-lock/WAL/rollback-journal path described in EmbeddedTransactionLock.cs, SqliteWalReadSnapshotCoordinator.cs, SqliteWalWriterCheckpointCoordinator.cs, and SqliteRollbackJournal.cs. Ahtola's model is therefore SQLite's classic single-writer/multiple-reader locking discipline exclusively: a single write reservation gate (EmbeddedTransactionLock, process-local, modeling SQLite's RESERVED/EXCLUSIVE locks with FIFO fairness for explicit transactions and barging for autocommit statements) and per-reader WAL snapshots (SqliteWalReadSnapshot pinning a committed WAL frame boundary) rather than a true multi-writer optimistic-concurrency layer. Adopting Turso's MVCC design would require: a new in-memory versioned row store keyed by (table, rowid) with begin/commit timestamps; a logical clock with the same atomicity guarantee as MvccClock; a write-write conflict detector integrated into VDBE Insert/Update/Delete opcode execution; a dual-cursor overlay so classic-path and MVCC-path connections observe correct visibility against each other; a durable logical-log + checkpoint-into-WAL story so MVCC state survives restart; row-version garbage collection; and new parser/VDBE support for `BEGIN CONCURRENT` as a per-transaction mode alongside the existing DEFERRED/IMMEDIATE/EXCLUSIVE. This is a multi-week/-month undertaking (L effort, likely several L-sized sub-projects) and is reasonably deferrable relative to correctness gaps elsewhere, since Ahtola's classic-path transactions already give SQLite-compatible single-writer serializable-enough semantics for the vast majority of consumer workloads;       it is filed s2-capability (a real missing capability, not yet proven to be an intentional non-goal) pending an explicit product decision to scope it out. Wave F2.9 (2026-08-06) redistributed two corpus keys here after PRAGMA wal_checkpoint became a supported classic-path operation: the mvcc-delete-via-index and mvcc-idxdelete-exact-seek tests now get past the pragma and fail on their underlying `PRAGMA journal_mode=mvcc` assertion (expected 'mvcc' but got 'memory'/'wal').

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/mvcc/clock.rs::MvccClock, LogicalClock::get_timestamp/get_commit_timestamp
gaps.notes: Turso's MvccClock is a mutex-guarded monotonic counter where the commit-timestamp generation and publication of the transaction's Preparing(ts) state happen atomically under one lock (documented at length in clock.rs to close a proven snapshot-isolation TOCTOU bug from an earlier lock-free attempt, turso#5198). Ahtola has no logical clock concept in its transaction model; its WAL snapshot coordinator (SqliteWalReadSnapshotCoordinator.cs) pins a *frame* boundary rather than a logical timestamp, which is adequate for the classic pager path but has no analogue for a future MVCC begin_ts/commit_ts scheme. Any MVCC implementation must budget for this atomicity requirement explicitly, not bolt a naive counter on afterward.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/mvcc/database/mod.rs::LimboError::WriteWriteConflict (raised at multiple sites, e.g. lines ~1843, ~1865-1976, ~2798, ~5191-5227)
gaps.notes: Turso's MVCC path detects first-committer-wins write-write conflicts and surfaces LimboError::WriteWriteConflict distinctly from Busy, so callers can decide whether to retry (Busy, lock contention) or must restart the transaction with new reads (WriteWriteConflict, logical conflict). Ahtola's whole-database EmbeddedTransactionLock model makes write-write conflicts structurally impossible to observe as a distinct error: only one writer can ever hold the reservation at a time, so overlapping writers serialize via EmbeddedBusyException (SQLITE_BUSY) rather than racing and one aborting after the fact. This is consistent with the classic single-writer model and not a bug, but it means Ahtola cannot express Turso's MVCC concurrent-write semantics (multiple writers proceeding optimistically) without introducing this conflict-detection concept.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/mvcc/database/mod.rs::drop_unused_row_versions, drop_unused_row_versions_and_slots, drop_unused_row_versions_inner (lines ~6995-7275)
gaps.notes: Turso's MVCC store accumulates multiple row versions per key and periodically garbage-collects versions no longer visible to any active transaction (three-rule pruning, driven opportunistically from the commit path and test loops). gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/execute.rs (Transaction/AutoCommit opcode arms, TransactionMode::None/Read/Write/Concurrent)
gaps.notes: Ahtola's actual (non-MVCC) transaction model is itself undocumented at a design level: it is a single process-local write reservation (EmbeddedTransactionLock, one lock per file-backed database keyed by canonicalized path via EmbeddedTransactionLockRegistry, or one per in-memory database instance) that models SQLite's RESERVED/EXCLUSIVE locks, with FIFO fairness for explicit-transaction writers (Enter) but barging for autocommit statements (EnterAutocommit) to avoid a documented starvation bug (ENGINE #17, EF migrations-lock convoy). Readers pin a WAL frame/page-count snapshot via SqliteWalReadSnapshotCoordinator/SqliteWalReadSnapshot rather than a logical timestamp. SqlTransactionControl.cs is a lightweight lexical scanner (not a parser integration) that Ahtola.Data uses to detect COMMIT/END/ROLLBACK[ TO] keywords in raw SQL text for ADO.NET-level transaction bookkeeping. None of this is written down anywhere as a coherent isolation-level statement (e.g. 'Ahtola provides snapshot-isolated reads against a single active writer, equivalent to SQLite's default WAL-mode semantics'); this entry exists to flag that documentation gap alongside the code gaps, since accurately characterizing the current model was itself part of this audit's scope.
